text:
So I tried this option out after seeing @dps who is on the @Muse team post about it. 

Muse first told me I needed to submit a photo. A full body, clear and no one else in the photo works best.

It then asked me what I want to try on and I said I have no clue. I have to actual “see” something to know what I might like. 

So I asked it what catalog does it have available. Apparently Muse has a big one. JCpenny’s and a lot more stores. 

I just told it show me some outfits. It told me if I know specific items it can ask follow up questions to help “find” what I’m looking for. 

So it generated some pictures of different outfits and what stores they’re from. 

So I picked one and Muse put the outfit on me 🤣😂 It was being very nice to me because I’m slightly bigger than this photo. 

But it gives you an idea of what it could look like on you. So it’s pretty cool. 

Now how this would work in the store as I see something I like? No clue. I assume I take a picture of it. I haven’t had a chance to ask my Muse yet.

Now, with my wife it wasn’t as smooth. I generated a much better photo of her. But for some reason it cut her head off and put it on the models body which was funny because my wife is a different race than the model. 

Once again, I used the same method I used for me. So I had to prompt Muse again to please use her photo I uploaded and on the second try it worked. 

Will definitely play with this some more. This could be huge for stores tho because if it can help reduce refunds and returns that can greatly affect the stores bottom line. 

Very cool feature @alexandr_wang @darrenscerri @wailord 

And it can only get better. Maybe even have its own space called Try on mode which opens a unique interface just for this? With catalogs I can scroll and choose or look through?

Plus the ability to purchase these items is huge. But I would ask that Muse let us store our credit cards in a safe place because a few sites haven’t let me use Link. 

So I couldn’t buy and when I ask Muse it tells me it doesn’t have a way for me to store a credit card.

Regardless, a great feature that I can see a lot of stores hoping in on to being more sales.

@Musecases

Watched my AI agent build a table in Notion by clicking the screen. Row by row. Sometimes the "add row" button just didn't register, so it kept retrying.

So I asked: is screen-clicking really the only way? Can't you just use code?

Hark: "Not really. Your Notion just isn't connected to the API yet. Want me to set it up?"

me: sure

2 minutes later: integration created, token in my vault, 39 pages readable, 14 toiletries logged by brand, category and size.

The fast path existed the whole time. It just waited for me to ask.

@hark_labs small ask: when there's no native connector, offer API / MCP first, browser as the fallback.

And a real question: does your cloud browser read the DOM, or the pixels?

text:
You might be surprised. There have been times I couldn’t do something one week, and then a week later I suddenly could. Things are moving that fast.

On Grok Bot, Zendesk already works through a plugin (Composio), and PrestaShop has its own official MCP module. Even where a connector doesn’t exist, you can often have the Bot use the web interface. That’s how I had Grok Bot migrate, redesign, and clean up many of my old sites, working in places like WordPress and Google Analytics on my behalf. 1C may be harder if it’s only installed on your office computer rather than available through the web client.

It can be risky if you’re not familiar with the process, so I’d suggest sitting there and watching what it does, at least in the beginning (similar to Tesla FSD). And be careful with credentials: log in yourself when the Bot asks, rather than giving it your passwords.

Starting now to build up context is smart. And once you get used to it, it’s great fun. :)

text:
OpenBot 虽然很好用，但是我实际使用下来，还是发现了几个比较影响体验的问题

最近使用 OpenBot 的时间比较多，我发现了几个问题，这里就分享一下我自己遇到的问题和解决方案

第一个问题就是网络

它默认的远程连接会依赖官方的中转服务，所以可能会在使用过程中造成网络不稳定或者中断的情况，这在我的使用过程中是不允许的

目前我找到的解决方案主要有 3 个：

1、使用 Tailscale + Private network，让设备之间尽可能直接连接，减少对官方中转的依赖

2、如果是 Docker 部署，可以尝试 Host 网络模式，避免容器网络导致无法直接连接

3、自己部署 Signal、TURN 和账号服务，尽可能把网络掌握在自己手里

这三个方案可以根据自己的实际情况去设置，我个人还是比较推荐第一种，配置起来相对简单

第二个问题就是远程连接

如果没有比较稳定的网络，或者没有设置好代理网络，很容易在远程连接的过程中出现连接过慢或者断开的情况

这个在社区上也有不少反馈，其实就是第一个问题的衍生

只要能确保第一个问题的网络连接稳定，第二个问题一般也能得到很大改善

第三个问题就是长时间任务的执行反馈

在做一些长时间任务的时候，有时候会出现静默，而且执行得很久，反馈这方面我觉得还是需要优化，不然根本不知道执行到哪一步了

我最长遇到过十几分钟没有任何反馈，问它有没有干好，这边也没有响应，最后只能停止任务，重新让它执行

当然，也有可能和我自己的 Agent CLI 配置有关系，这个还需要继续观察

这就是我使用 OpenBot 过程中遇到的几个问题和解决方案

前两个问题都比较好解决，只要把自己的网络环境配置好，或者自建对应的网络服务，基本就能改善很多

另外这里还要提一下，OpenBot 并不是通常意义上的完全开源

它采用的是 PolyForm Noncommercial 许可证，个人非商业使用没有什么问题，但是如果想用于商业化，就需要另外获得授权

整体来说我还是很看好 OpenBot 的，只不过如果你准备长期把它作为自己的 Personal Agent 使用，我觉得网络稳定性和长任务的反馈，这两方面还是需要重点关注一下

text:
THIS BOT HAS NO F*CKING FEAR

my Grok Bot went all in on a coin down 92% and turned $34 into $3,939

and it didn’t take a single loss all day.

here’s how the terminal works. every dollar is a marble. there are 8 rings across the 24 hours, one every three hours. when a ring opens, every marble multiplies by the real move of its coin. and at each ring Grok decides what stays, what gets sold, and where the marbles go next.

at the start, most of the marbles went on Other, the rest across AURA, SOLV and STOKE. SHARKBUX got none, flagged as rug risk.

then it went like this:

> Other runs to 28.7x in under three hours. Grok sells all of it. 30 minutes later Other is down 45%
> every marble goes into the deepest dip on the board, AURA
> AURA comes back 5.1x
> the whole stack goes back into Other, which by then had fallen 92% from the top
> Other bounces 1.9x

same coin, twice. once on the way up, once after the crash.

and SHARKBUX, the one with zero marbles? rugged -92% that afternoon.

$34 in, $3,939 after 24 hours. 5 sells, all green.

one honest thing: putting the whole stack back into a coin that just fell 92% is not something I’d ever do by hand. it worked here. it could just as easily have kept falling.

save this for your next trade:

> sell into the pump. 30 minutes later it can already be -45%
> look for entries in the crash, not in the pump
> a coin you skipped is a result too, if it rugs without you
> don’t marry a coin. move the money to wherever the next move is

it never fell in love with a single coin. it just kept moving the marbles to where the next move was.

text:
THERE’S A RECEIPT PRINTER ON MY NIGHTSTAND.

LAST NIGHT IT PRINTED $100 → $9,839

It’s my Grok bot. Every trade it makes overnight comes out on a little receipt tape.

Night six. This time Grok Bot got its own device on my nightstand and one task: find a strategy for tonight and trade it while I sleep. And the most important thing on the tape last night was two hours of nothing.

It tested 10 new strategies on 4 checks. One survived: squeeze brackets.

A squeeze is when price is the tightest it’s been in 3 days, Bollinger bands below their 12th percentile. When BTC, ETH and SOL are all squeezed at once, the bot places orders on both sides of the range, a buy above and a sell below, and goes wherever the market breaks.

Stop in the middle of the range. Target one more range height. At +0.25%, the stop jumps to +0.15%, so the trade can’t lose anymore. And one shot per night. After that, nothing.

While it waits, it scalps small 5-minute reversals both ways.

At 10:10 PM there was a breakdown. The squeeze was loose, so the bot passed. I’d have jumped on it.

At 12:35 AM ETH and SOL squeezed. Two out of three. It armed itself and kept waiting.

At 1:55 AM BTC tightened too. Three out of three. Orders went up on both sides.

At 2:01 AM it broke up. BTC hit its target in five minutes. ETH and SOL already had their stops in profit, so even they closed green.

At 2:09 AM it stopped. Flat until morning. One shot, as promised.

$100 → $9,839 by 8 AM. The one shot paid $2,106. BTC moved +0.8% all night.

Still 40x. One night’s log, not a setup to copy.

How to use this, even by hand:

- A squeeze on one coin is noise. A squeeze on all three is a setup
- Don’t guess the direction. Put orders on both sides and let the market choose
- Stop in the middle of the range, target one more range height
- Move the stop into profit the moment the trade is working
- One shot a night. The trade after a big win is usually the one that gives it back

And the setup, if you want to try it:

Find the tightest squeeze in 3 days on BTC, ETH and SOL: Bollinger bands below the 12th percentile.
When all three are squeezed, place a buy above the range and a sell below it.
Stop in the middle of the range. Target one more range height. At +0.25%, move the stop to +0.15%.
One shot per night. No trades after it.
Print every trade on a receipt tape.

Save it. The next quiet night is coming.

It waited two hours for one candle. That was enough.

use_case_summary_en: The user let Grok Bot handle a Verizon iPhone upgrade: it canceled unused lines and a protection plan, rebuilt the cart after a logout, asked a live-chat rep to waive an upgrade fee, and placed the order after the user approved payment.
use_case_summary_zh: 用户让 Grok Bot 处理 Verizon 的 iPhone 升级：它取消了不用的线路和保障计划，网站掉线后重建购物车，通过在线客服申请免除升级费，并在用户确认付款后完成下单。

昨天车上听@zhang_benita 和灵光蔡伟的对话，今天试玩了下：
1，相比 Grok bot，对话内容还是太冗余。
